chapter.title: Getting in and standing up

cards.body: Most beginners don't panic because they sink. They panic because they can't find their feet. Think of the water as a bed you lie on, not a floor you fall through: your body already floats, and this whole handbook is about letting it. **Chapter 1 is how to get off the bed**: knees in, hands down, feet on the floor, every time.
cards.simpler: Most new swimmers don't panic because they go under. They panic because they can't find their feet. Picture the water as a bed you lie on, not a floor you fall through. Your body already floats on its own. This handbook is about letting it. **Chapter 1 is how to get off the bed**: pull your knees in, push your hands down, put your feet on the floor. Every single time.

cards.prompt: Priya is lying face down in chest-deep water, holding the wall. She lets go and her feet float up behind her. She wants to stand. What's her first move?

options.text: Kick her legs down hard to find the floor
Pull her knees in to her chest
Lift her head and grab for the wall

whyNot.a: That's the long shape, not the ball: straight legs turn slowly, so kicking down just splashes while her feet stay up.
whyNot.c: That's reaching, not standing: the wall is further away than the floor, and lifting the head first leaves her legs trailing behind.

cards.reteach: Water holds a long body flat, like a bed holds you. To get up, make yourself small. Knees to chest turns you into a ball, and a ball rolls upright on its own, so your feet swing down underneath you.

cards.title: Getting in
cards.body:
Use the steps or the ladder, and go in *facing the ladder*, the way you'd climb down from a bunk bed. One hand stays on the rail until both feet are on the bottom. The pool floor is colder and smoother than you expect, so give your feet a second before you let go.

Now walk. Chest-deep water pushes back on every step, like wading through a crowd. Lean a little forward, take wide slow steps, and sweep your arms through the water ahead of you. **You can't fall through a bed.** Ten metres across, ten metres back.
cards.simpler:
Use the steps or ladder, and go in facing the ladder, like climbing down from a bunk bed. Keep one hand on the rail until both feet touch the bottom. The pool floor feels colder and smoother than you expect, so give your feet a second before letting go.

Now walk. Chest-deep water pushes back on each step, like moving through a crowd. Lean forward a little, take wide slow steps, and sweep your arms through the water. **You can't fall through a bed.** Ten metres across, ten metres back.

cards.title: Marcus stands up
cards.body: Marcus, first lesson, a council pool on a Tuesday night. He walks the width fine, then holds the wall and lets his legs float up behind him, like lying face down on a mattress. He lets go. Feet up, face in, and his brain declares an emergency. He thrashes for 3 seconds. Then he does what the teacher said: knees in, hands press down, feet find the tiles. He stands. The water reaches his chest. **He has been drowning in 1.2 metres.**
cards.simpler: Marcus is at his first lesson, a council pool on a Tuesday night. He walks the width with no trouble. Then he holds the wall and lets his legs float up behind him, like lying face down on a mattress. He lets go. Feet up, face in, and his brain shouts danger. He thrashes for 3 seconds. Then he does what the teacher said: knees in, hands press down, feet find the tiles. He stands. The water reaches his chest. **He has been drowning in 1.2 metres.**

cards.prompt: You're face down in the shallow end, hands off the wall, feet floating up. Which order gets you standing calmly?

options.text: Knees to chest, press both hands down toward the floor, plant your feet, then lift your head
Lift your head high first, then straighten your legs and feel for the floor with your toes
Spread your arms wide and wait for your feet to sink on their own

whyNot.b: That's the long shape again: straightening your legs keeps you flat on the bed, and a flat body is slow to turn upright.
whyNot.c: That's floating, not standing: wide arms keep you lying on the surface, which is chapter 3's job, not what you want right now.

cards.reteach: Three moves, in order: knees, hands, feet. Knees in makes you a ball. Hands pressing down lift your chest, so your hips drop under you. Now your feet are already below you, and you just put them down.

cards.title: Why the ball works
cards.body:
A long body lying on water is stable, like a plank on a bed: it wants to stay flat. A ball is not. Pull your knees in and the plank becomes a ball, and the heavy end, your hips and legs, swings down under you fast.

You'd think reaching for the floor with your toes is quickest. It's slowest, because it keeps you long. Press your hands down flat instead, like pushing a lid onto a box. Your chest rises, your feet land, and only then does your head come up.

**Knees, hands, feet, head.** Do it 10 times today, until your body does it before your brain can vote.
cards.simpler:
A long body lying on water is steady, like a plank on a bed. It wants to stay flat. A ball is not steady. Pull your knees in and the plank becomes a ball. Your heavy end, your hips and legs, swings down under you fast.

Reaching for the floor with your toes feels quickest. It's slowest, because it keeps you long. Press your hands down flat instead, like pushing a lid onto a box. Your chest rises, your feet land, then your head comes up.

**Knees, hands, feet, head.** Do it 10 times today, until your body moves before your brain can argue.

cards.body: Dana let go of the wall, felt her feet rise, and lunged sideways for the wall with both arms. She missed, swallowed a mouthful, and came up coughing. The wall was 1 metre away. The floor was 20 centimetres under her toes. Spot it in yourself: if your arms are reaching out or up instead of **pressing down**, you're trying to catch something instead of standing.
cards.simpler: Dana let go of the wall and felt her feet rise. She lunged sideways for the wall with both arms. She missed, swallowed a mouthful, and came up coughing. The wall was 1 metre away. The floor was 20 centimetres under her toes. Watch for this in yourself. If your arms are reaching out or up instead of **pressing down**, you're trying to grab something instead of standing up.

cards.prompt: A friend asks why pulling your knees in works. What's the real reason?

options.text: It makes you heavier, so you sink straight to the bottom
It turns your long flat body into a ball, and a ball rolls upright fast, so your feet swing underneath you
It squeezes air out of your lungs, so your chest drops

whyNot.a: That's weight, not shape: you weigh exactly the same tucked or stretched, it's the shape that changes how fast you turn.
whyNot.c: That's breath, not shape: your lungs stay full while you tuck, and letting air out is the next chapter's job, not this one's.

cards.reteach: Water holds a flat body flat, like a bed. Make yourself small and the water can't hold you flat any more: your heavy hips drop, your feet come under you, and you stand.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
Water is a bed, not a floor: you climb in by the ladder, you can walk across it, and when you're lying on it and want up, you make a ball. **Knees, hands, feet, head**, under 2 seconds, so standing is always one move away.

Tomorrow: the first real swimming skill has nothing to do with moving. It's blowing bubbles.
cards.simpler:
Water is a bed, not a floor. You climb in by the ladder. You can walk across it. When you're lying on it and want to get up, you make a ball. **Knees, hands, feet, head**, in under 2 seconds. That way standing up is always one move away.

Tomorrow: the first real swimming skill has nothing to do with moving. It's blowing bubbles.

cards.body: Tonight, on your floor: lie face down, then pull your knees in, press your palms down, get your feet under you and stand. Time it. Do 5. Under 2 seconds each is the goal.
cards.simpler: Tonight, on your floor at home: lie face down. Then pull your knees in, press your palms down, get your feet under you and stand up. Time how long it takes. Do it 5 times. The goal is under 2 seconds each time.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now get into chest-deep water, walk across the pool, and stand up from lying forward in under 2 seconds, every time.
